name: The Point of Subtle Fire
previous_label: Utthita Parsvakonasana — Extended Side Angle (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: dhāmāntaḥkṣobhasambhūtasūkṣmāgnitilakākṛtim | binduṃ śikhānte hṛdaye layānte dhyāyato layaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: For one who meditates, at the top of the head or in the heart, on the bindu, a tilaka-like spark of subtle fire produced by agitation within the 'abode', there is dissolution at the end of dissolution.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh glosses the 'abode' (dhāma) as the light in the eyes and the agitation as pressure on the eyes. Bäumer has 'by agitating the eye', Chaudhri 'press the eyes gently' and Dubois 'une pression (exercée sur les yeux)' (all as printed in The Mystery Within). Singh offers an alternative: the sparks seen as a lamp goes out. Wallis renders it more neutrally as 'inner stimulation of the Radiant Abode'.

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y11 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.hatha_es: dharana 14 = the text of verse 43 (space in all directions); non-standard, not followed (the previous draft of this door followed it)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 37 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: a tiny spark of light (bindu) meditated at either place
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one tiny point of fire-like light, placed either at the top of the head or in the heart, that is watched until it dissolves. Observe-only because the classical trigger is pressure on the eyes.
geometry.svg_hint: a small red-gold dot at the crown and another at the heart, drawn faint; observe-only
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Spark to dissolution (observed)
reaction.summary: School metaphor: one spark of attention is watched until it goes out, and attention goes out with it. A picture for understanding, not an exercise.

breath.cue: Natural breath only. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; keep the eyes untouched and soft
orientation.gravity: Fully supported; hands resting away from the face
orientation.gaze: Eyes open, or closed without pressure
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: a tiny point of light at the crown or heart, watched until it dissolves
attention.secondary: If sitting with it: noticing any light that appears by itself behind closed eyes, without touching the eyes

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: For one who meditates, at the top of the head or in the heart, on the bindu, a tilaka-like spark of subtle fire produced by agitation within the 'abode', there is dissolution at the end of dissolution.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: produce a spark of light by pressure or agitation of the eyes, then meditate on it at the top of the head or in the heart until it dissolves. Observe-only in this school because the classical trigger is pressure on the eyes. Never press or rub the eyes. For practice with light and inner space, use Door 011 or Door 012.

honesty.disclosure: Door 014 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 14 (verse 37) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 014 is dharana 14, verse 37. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.
historical/observe_only: The classical trigger for the spark of light is pressure on, or agitation of, the eyes. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.
Numbering correction: the previous draft of this door followed hatha.es's non-standard numbering (dharana 14 = the text of verse 43 (space in all directions)). Rebuilt to Singh's verse 37.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. [retired posture] and VBT dharana 014 are paired by school index so students can braid a strong side-body geometry with an omnidirectional space contemplation.
legacy.notes: Experiential resonance (not canon): the [retired posture]’s vivid one-sided stretch can highlight the habit of locating awareness in a solid edge; dharana 014 then invites space in all directions at once. Kept as school_device because the serial index pairing is the School’s primary rule.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Never press or rub the eyes to produce light. This school does not teach eye pressure in any form. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Hands-on-hips side bend in a shorter stance, or [retired posture] with soft side stretch; use a block under the bottom hand rather than reaching the floor.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease off if front knee, hip, or neck complains; shorten stance and raise the bottom hand.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

safety.observe_only_note: Never press or rub the eyes to produce light. This school does not teach eye pressure in any form.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 014: the point of subtle fire. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 14, verse 37. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit comfortably, hands away from the face. The map is one tiny point of light, at the crown or in the heart.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Keep the eyes soft and untouched. Eyes open, or closed without pressure.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the idea: one spark, watched until it goes out.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a spark of attention goes out, and attention goes with it. A picture, not an exercise.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 37: meditate on a spark of subtle fire at the crown or in the heart until it dissolves. Classically the spark comes from pressure on the eyes, so this door is observe-only. Never press the eyes.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Open the eyes and look at something far away. Move on when ready.
